details: Bitcoin has dropped to approximately $61,000-$62,000, marking its lowest level in four months. This downturn is attributed to significant and continuous net outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs, which have surpassed $2.5 billion in cumulative outflows for November 2026. Further contributing to the pressure are expectations of continued Federal Reserve interest rate hikes and a broad sell-off in traditional stock markets, with some investor capital seemingly rotating into the highly successful initial public offering (IPO) of AI firm Anthropic.
title: Bitcoin Plunges Amid ETF Outflows, Fed Rate Hike Fears & Anthropic IPO

details: Ethereum's price has declined, trading below $1,800, mirroring the broader market downturn. Further dampening sentiment, the highly anticipated "Glamsterdam" network upgrade has been postponed until at least January 2027. Developers cited critical smart contract compatibility issues as the reason for the delay, highlighting ongoing challenges in balancing innovation with ecosystem stability. U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs have also seen a sustained period of net outflows.
title: Ethereum Falls, 'Glamsterdam' Upgrade Delayed to 2027

details: Esteemed commodity trader Peter Brandt has issued a cautious outlook for Bitcoin, suggesting that the leading cryptocurrency could face further substantial losses. Brandt's analysis points to a recurring historical pattern where major bull runs conclude with significant market corrections, potentially implying a full 75% correction from Bitcoin's October 2025 peak. This warning comes as Bitcoin struggles to regain momentum after its recent pullback.
title: Veteran Trader Peter Brandt Warns of Deeper Bitcoin Correction
